entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Hayne van Ghizeghem was a Franco-Flemish composer of the early Renaissance Burgundian School, active in the court of Philip the Good in 1430s-1450s. He was a key figure in the development of the Franco-Flemish school, alongside Josquin des Prez and John Dunstaple. His music reflects the influence of Burgundian courtly culture and the emerging humanist ideals of the time. Through his compositions, van Ghizeghem helped shape the musical landscape of 15th-century Europe, leaving a lasting legacy in the world of Renaissance music.

The exact dates of van Ghizeghem's birth and death are unknown, but his compositions suggest he was active during the 1430s-1450s. His music was widely performed in the Burgundian court and beyond, influencing later generations of composers. The Franco-Flemish school, to which van Ghizeghem belonged, was a major force in the development of Western classical music.

Despite his significant contributions to music, van Ghizeghem's life remains somewhat of a mystery. His compositions continue to be performed and studied today, a testament to his enduring legacy.

In 1476, van Ghizeghem died in the service of Philip the Good, his music having already made a lasting impact on the musical landscape of Europe.
